lines.text: I woke up on a mudbank, coughing up half the Senn. Somebody had built a fire. It was a very bad fire. It was the most beautiful thing I'd ever seen.
Ash lay beside me, steaming. Someone had pulled the bolt out of his shoulder and packed the wound with river moss.
Lord Lucan Varr. Half drowned, in the mud, at my feet. I've dreamed of this moment for a year. I'd imagined enjoying it more.
Long pale hair, filthy now. A black steward's coat in rags. On its chest, a crow brooch had been torn away, and left a clean little ghost of itself in the dirt.
The last time I'd seen him, he had thirty sellswords and a forged clause nine.
Steward Corvin.
Just Corvin now. Lady Sabine let me go after the war. She said the forged clause was my idea. She wrote it herself, of course. I only carried it.
Ash lifted his head and looked at him. Corvin went very still.
In my defence, my lord, when I said kill the dog first, I meant it professionally.

One by one, the river had spat the others onto his mudbank, and he'd dragged them out of the reeds. Wren, with Granny's axe still on her back. Tamsin and Ilse, holding each other up. And Oswin, in his shirt.
Eleven years I had that breastplate. Eleven years. The Senn can choke on it.
My lord, this man tried to steal Greyhollow.
He also pulled me out of a river. It's been a complicated year.
I asked him why he'd done it. He poked his terrible fire for a long time before he answered.
I kept House Corrow's books for twelve years, my lord. Every crown in, every crown out. Nobody hires a steward who knows that much. So I came to the river. Where things wash up.
There was one payment, you know. Every quarter-day. To a house with no name. I was never allowed to write it down.
Can you still keep books?
Better than anyone alive. That was always the trouble.
Then you're hired. The pay is terrible. Breakfast is mostly goat. And you'll be working for a zero.
My lord, I worked for a crow for twelve years. A zero will be a holiday.
In the reeds downstream, Tamsin found Tobin's crate, dry as a bone. Wren had kicked it off the wagon on her way past. Of course it floated. Tobin had built it to float. Just in case.
The Hounds would be watching every road to Aldcrown. Corvin knew a better way.
The safest house on this river, my lord, is the one no Hound would dare to knock on.
Whose?
Your father's.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter sixty-five, coming soon.
